Update 2026.01.11: Upladed a new hull and forecastle, as the assembly of the main deck was not possible without some extra work in the original version.

You will have to print the back wheel parts twice for a complete model.
The model is separated into a couple of separate parts to simplify painting it. If you feel brave enough to paint it as a single piece, then just import the stl files in a 3D editor, most of the parts should be in ther correct positions. You will have to duplicate and position the right back wheel parts though.

A 10mm scale Marienburg landship for Warmaster. With crew. I scaled it to a regular Warmaster base, that made it roughly as large as a steam tank, so it can be an alternative for the warmachine. The crew is not merged to the other parts, so it is relatively easy to separate them if you would like to resize the ship. Rescaling it to 140% would fit a 40x60 base.

LennyFace asked me to do a landship last year. I always like to fiddle with machines. It means I usually don't have to rely on other miniatures or AI, just pure modeling fun. Though in this case I used a couple of sources...

This was a fun little model - the Doomguard Rot Blade. It's a CR6 with a very nasty ability that, on kill, turns a creature and their non-magic items to ash. This is pretty brutal. Now I'm not sure on the ruling if that negates death saving throws as well but regardless it's nasty.

👍 Don't forget to Like and Collect this, so you can easily find it later! ⭐
If you like my models and what I do then come follow me on Patreon https://www.patreon.com/c/Adamnant for updates on my quests and access to exclusive minis.

This started as an AI model that I posed and sculpted, added spears, sword and helmet to. The helmet was something I had to kinda make from scratch. I think it looks pretty good. Here is a full video of my work on this model: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xc8zzAErLSc

There are 3x variants of this mini. One with a pointing pose, one two-handed sword attack pose and one javelin throwing pose.

For printing I think the large version will be fine on FDM but like my previous model you'll want to be mindful of the spear. There are a few small surfaces and horns so it could be a bit of pain when removing supports on FDM but I believe in you! Just make sure to rotate the model so that supports aren't wrapped around the spear and you should be good. For resin I think auto-supports will work completely fine - just tilt it back 45 degrees.

I've completed my quest for 1000 models in 2025 so now I'm trying to decide whats next. You can follow along with me on Thingiverse, Printables, Cults3d or provide suggestions on Patreon here: https://www.patreon.com/c/Adamnant (as well as get codes for exclusive downloads on Cults3d). If you have something that you need or a custom model like this that you want then let me know and let's make it!

I recently finished the Relic Sloth model and part of that included some various packs / bags / bedrolls etc... so I wanted to make sure those were available as separate items as well. You can find the relic Sloth here: https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:7202569

The bag of coins originates from my bag jelly model as well over here: https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:7192928

In here I've got 5 x different packs and a bedroll as well as 2x arrangements. You can print out the whole versions, sliced/flattened versions or the arrangements.

Edit: Update Nov 24, I played around and remade the giant space hamster bag by hand. I've added a huge, large and medium version of that bag / pack to this collection. Also added a grain sack / bag with ropes around it.

These are fairly low detail models because they're so small. They could absolutely be 1,000,000 vertices and have details on all the straps and clips etc... but that's not very likely to show up on prints (and there are many other high fidelity pack models out there if you want that). This set will get the "scatter" job done and won't stress out your printer in the process.

I've completed my quest for 1000 models in 2025 so now I'm trying to decide whats next. Here is a Blood Hunter miniature based on the artwork from Explorer's Guide to Wildemount. I had a request for one of these so I put it together and then realized the request was for a changeling Blood Hunter - whoops. I guess I've gotta go back to making another blood hunter model. Technically changelings can take any shape or form so maybe this one works too. Aside from that there doesn't seem to be much for what changelings should look like in their unchanged form.

This was made with AI using a service called Rodin and I brought that into blender and sculpted some of the details into it, fixed a broken hand and other wonky topology.

Full VOD:
- Part 1 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pQIonB5CrdQ
- Part 2 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IocXjSpu1JQ

I'm on a quest to make 1000 dnd models in 2025 and you can join me on Thingiverse, Printables, Cults3d or see my weekly updates on Patreon here: https://www.patreon.com/c/Adamnant (as well as get codes for exclusive downloads on Cults3d). I'm focusing on models that don't seem to exist on Printables / Thingiverse and are listed in campaigns. If you have something that you need or a custom model like this that you want then let me know and let's make it!

- 1.15mm thick paperclip (1.25mm hole)

Besides Warmaster, Mordheim was the other Specialist Games wargame I always wanted to sink into. I had the chance to play a few games with my club back then, but the interest faded away in the group. I though it would be interesting to check whether it works in 10mm so I quickly assembled a Reiklander mercenary warband for testing purposes. I guess these will not be that useful for others, the minis are quite specific, but at lest they can be useful if I ever want to do an empire Warmaster army.

Here is the roster:
Captain - sword, pistol (85)
Champion - halberd, bow (55)
Champion - halberd (45)
Youngblood - spear, bow (35)
Youngblood - spear, bow (35)
4 Marksman - crossbow (4x50)

All armed gangers are either on 5.8mm round inserts or without such inserts. Note that the 25mm bases are just the bases, not the insert detail bits from the separate kit.

These cannot be used for commercial purposes unless you buy the commercial license on my Gumroad site.


From the wikipedia page on Ronin
n feudal Japan (1185–1868), a rōnin (/ˈroʊnɪn/ ROH-nin; Japanese: 浪人, IPA: [ɾoːɲiɴ], 'drifter' or 'wanderer', lit. 'a person of the waves')[1] was a samurai who had no lord or master and in some cases, had also severed all links with his family or clan. A samurai becomes a rōnin upon the death of his master, or after the loss of his master's favor or legal privilege.[2][3]

In modern Japanese, the term is usually used to describe a salaryman who is unemployed or a secondary school graduate who has not yet been admitted to university.[4][5]
Etymology

The word rōnin is usually translated to 'drifter' or 'wanderer'; however, per kanji, rō (浪) means "wave" (as in body of water) or "unrestrained", while nin (人) means "man" or "person". It is an idiomatic expression for 'vagrant' or 'wandering man', someone who finds the way without belonging to one place. The term originated in the Nara and Heian periods, when it referred to a serf who had fled or deserted his master's land. In medieval times, the Ronin were depicted as the shadows of samurai, master-less and less honorable. It then came to be used for a samurai who had no master (hence the term 'wave man' illustrating one who is socially adrift).[3]
Status

According to the Bushido Shoshinshu (the "Code of the Warrior"), a samurai was supposed to commit seppuku (also harakiri, "belly cutting", a form of ritual suicide) upon the loss of his master.[6][7] One who chose not to honor the code was "on his own" and was meant to suffer great shame. The undesirability of rōnin status was mainly a discrimination imposed by other samurai and by daimyō, the feudal lords.[citation needed]

Like other samurai, rōnin wore two swords.[8] Rōnin used a variety of other weapons as well. Some rōnin—usually those who lacked money—would carry a bō (staff around 1.5 to 1.8 m (5 to 6 ft)) or jō (smaller staff or walking stick around 0.9 to 1.5 m (3 to 5 ft)) or a yumi (bow). Most weapons would reflect the ryū (martial arts school) from which they came if they were students.[citation needed]

During the Edo period, with the shogunate's rigid class system and laws, the number of rōnin greatly increased. Confiscation of fiefs during the rule of the third Tokugawa shōgun Iemitsu resulted in an especially large increase of rōnin.[2] During previous ages, samurai were able to move between masters and even between occupations. They could also marry between classes. However, during the Edo period, samurai were restricted, and were—above all—forbidden to become employed by another master without their previous master's permission.[citation needed]

Because the former samurai could not legally take up a new trade, or because of pride were loath to do so, many rōnin looked for other ways to make a living with their swords. Those rōnin who desired steady, legal employment became mercenaries that guarded trade caravans, or bodyguards for wealthy merchants. Many other rōnin became criminals, operating as bandits and highwaymen, or joining organized crime in towns and cities. Rōnin were known to operate or serve as hired muscle for gangs that ran gambling rings, brothels, protection rackets, and similar activities. Many were petty thieves and muggers. The criminal segment gave the rōnin of the Edo period a persistent reputation of disgrace, with an image of thugs, bullies, cutthroats, and wandering vagrants.[2] After the abolition of the Samurai, some of the ronin continued with their thuggery and their mercenary work and activities, such as participating in the infamous assassination of Korean Empress Myeongseong of the Joseon Dynasty in 1895, the Eulmi Incident.[citation needed]
History
Graves of the forty-seven rōnin at Sengaku-ji

Until the Sengoku period, peasants accounted for the majority of daimyō armies, so they accounted for the majority of ronin.[citation needed]

Especially in the Sengoku period, daimyō needed additional fighting men, and even if a master had perished, his rōnin was able to serve new lords. In contrast to the later Edo period, the bond between the lord and the vassal was loose, and some vassals who were dissatisfied with their treatment left their masters and sought new lords. Many warriors served a succession of masters, and some even became daimyō. As an example, Tōdō Takatora served ten lords. Additionally, the division of the population into classes had not yet taken place, so it was possible to change one's occupation from warrior to merchant or farmer, or the reverse. Saitō Dōsan was one merchant who rose through the warrior ranks to become a daimyō.[citation needed]

As Toyotomi Hideyoshi unified progressively more significant parts of the country, daimyō found it unnecessary to recruit new soldiers. The Battle of Sekigahara in 1600 resulted in the confiscation or reduction of the fiefs of large numbers of daimyō on the losing side; consequently, many samurai became rōnin. As many as a hundred thousand rōnin joined forces with Toyotomi Hideyori and fought at the Siege of Osaka. In the ensuing years of peace, there was less need to maintain expensive standing armies, and many surviving rōnin turned to farms or became townspeople. A few, such as Yamada Nagamasa, sought adventure overseas as mercenaries. Still, the majority lived in poverty as rōnin. Their number approached half a million under the third Tokugawa shōgun Iemitsu.[citation needed]

Initially, the shogunate viewed them as dangerous and banished them from the cities or restricted the quarters where they could live. They also prohibited serving new masters. As rōnin found fewer options, they joined in the Keian Uprising of 1651. This forced the shogunate to rethink its policy. It relaxed restrictions on daimyō inheritance, resulting in fewer confiscations of fiefs, and it permitted rōnin to join new masters.[citation needed]

Not having the status or power of employed samurai, rōnin were often disreputable and festive,[2] the group targeted humiliation or satire. It was undesirable to be a rōnin, as it meant being without a stipend or land. As an indication of the shame felt by samurai who became rōnin, Lord Redesdale recorded that a rōnin killed himself at the graves of the forty-seven rōnin. He left a note saying that he had tried to enter the service of the daimyō of Chōshū Domain but was refused. He killed himself, wanting to serve no other master and hating being a rōnin. On the other hand, the famous 18th-century writer Kyokutei Bakin renounced his allegiance to Matsudaira Nobunari, in whose service Bakin's samurai father had spent his life. Bakin voluntarily became a rōnin, and eventually spent his time writing books (many of them about samurai) and engaging in festivities.[citation needed]

In the 19th century, Emperor Meiji abolished the Samurai class and any status the ronin had died with them.[citation needed]

Gotrek was another story. You play role-playing games or maybe miniature games (the fun ones with the narrative as central), maybe you play both or some hybrid of the two. So you must find yourself occasionally needing some good guys or bad guys to add to the mayhem. Maybe they are unscrupulous gunmen sent by a local crime boss. Maybe they are stalwart citizens ready to defend their town/neighborhood. Maybe they are the latest member of your space faring crew of adventurers, though you just haven't gotten to know them yet. Maybe they are just hired muscle with guns that your gang hired for a bit of extra firepower in the upcoming battle. Maybe they are just random survivors of the Zombie Apocalypse who could be potential friends or foes. The possibilities are endless for a basic miniature with a firearm (call it a rifle, carbine, or lasgun in this case), some light 'flak' armor, and a combat knife. These NPCs might not be the heroes of the day, but they can't be completely ignored either.

Greetings after many weeks! Finally, I am glad to present you the first wargame miniature based on the new setting. From this moment on, I step on thin ice, switching to artistic descriptions, being not a specialist in the mastery of words, and also not being an English-speaking person. I will try not to disappoint my subscribers and share the details of the setting as much as possible. I hope in the future I will be able to create an English-language resource where you can fully appreciate the idea, but for now keep a small piece that specifically affects these guys:

"The main source of raw materials for the alchemical industry of the Diamute people are ubiquitous deep layers of rock - necrolite formed by the remains of creatures of an ancient civilization.

The ancients were beings of a high order, capable of using magic, including flesh magic. With her help, the Haruspices, magicians of the flesh, built entire cities from the bodies and souls of specially grown donors (thus formed a significant part of the necrolite known today). Particularly guilty slaves and criminals also became donors of bodies for the research of Haruspices, which was a rather cruel and grotesque type of execution. Now the remnants of this civilization, known to humans as demons, inhabit the Bowels - an unlimited labyrinth of underground structures built by the Ancients.

The incessant mining of necrolite deposits often leads to clashes between miners and demons. The model you see represents such a getter. His life support suit is designed for long, deep expeditions into the Bowels. The power circuits are saturated with alchemical solutions that endow miners with supernatural endurance, but adversely affect their minds and souls. Armor plates and a sophisticated frame allow miners to withstand heavy loads of heavy and dangerous work with necrolite, as well as resist groups of younger demons waiting for miners in the endless spaces of the Bowels."

"Every battlefield the Hostile Environment Troops find themselves on, is a hostile, bombarded and chemically saturated one. Taking trenches, cities and sectors require troops in the thousands, and waiting for weeks or months on end for the right moment to strike. To that end, Command uses Shock Assault Troops, Specialists in lightning warfare.

Other armies decorate these soldiers in honors, having them as elite regiments on their planets. The best of the best.
Not so for the Hostile Environment Troops, for in the hellish condition they find themselves in, a simple hole in their suits means they are living on borrowed time.
Most, but not all, Shock Assault are penal legionaires, promised freedom if they survive a single attack on an enemy position. Very few survive to see reinforcements, fewer still survive long enough for a commissar to excuse them of their sins and turn them free men and women.

The life of a Shock Assault Trooper is a short and deadly life, but their sacrifices turn the tide of battle, saving thousands.

Enlist Today!"

This kit is a conversion kit for the newest plastic cadians. The torsos fit the equivelant piece in the assembling book in the plastic box.

there are
7 different heads
11 different torsos

All heads can be given female proportions by decreasing their width by roughly 8%

Note: Some cutting of the plastic legs are required

Using the fantastic model made by FELIXTHECRAZY (along another Ridgerunner proxy that dissapeared time ago and i dont know who made it), i designed this vehicle mostly for my Squat miners, but i think is suitable for Genestealers Cults too.

I cant assure if is a proper Ridgerunner proxy, because i think this model is smaller, but i added all the weapons and accesories listed in GSC army book for the vehicle in case that someone want to use it in that way. Maybe re-escaling it a bit is enough, but i dont how much, i have never seen a real Ridgerunner model before.

The original model is a single piece, meant to be printed in resin, but my experience printing vehicles in resin is not the best, so i prefer print them on PLA. With that in mind, i separated some pieces of the model to make it suitable for FDM printers, specially small parts that will probably break when you try to remove supports, then the best is print them apart and glue them after. Refer the pics to look where each piece goes

Weapons and accesories are small and detailed, and were designed to be printed in resin. You can try to print them in FDM of course, but they will lost a lot of detail, specially with the mining laser.

About the Spotter, i choose a more "technological" option instead a guy with binoculars. It makes more sense i think, and it saved me a lot of work :P

I included the center hull as one piece and in halves. I printed it as one piece, but I think it's easier and faster to print two pieces. Your choice.

I dont discard make some aditional weapons and accesories in the future.

Sci-fi troopers inspired by the 80's classics!

Currently included are lasguns, flamers, meltas, and plasma guns. There are 2 torso variants; one based on the original cover art by John Blanche (the vests), and one based on the actual models (with armor plates over the chest).

All the 15mm pre-assembled models are not merged, so you should be able to easily separate and customize them.

The separate parts will almost certainly NOT fit together if you print them separately. They are intended to be assembled digitally first.

Scale: The 15mm miniatures are a little more on the "heroic" side, about 16-16.5mm at the eye. The fits with many popular 15mm manufacturers, but if you want more "true scale" you should shrink them to about 95%. I have no idea about the 28mm scaling. I don't really own any 28mm miniatures any more.

Progress: There are currently only retro-style weapons, and open faced helmets. I'm planning on doing bare-heads, fully enclosed masks, and more modern style weapons very soon!

Credits:
ZIOCRU for the original bodies, legs, arms, and heads (heavily modified by me)
MrOrangeJumper - hands
MKHand_Industries - rifles, flamer, melta
dotplot (on thingiverse) - plasma

Here are twelve, perhaps crude, though definitely brutal close combat hand-to-hand melee assault weapons. They are intended to allow give you some extra options and conversion bits for your Chaos Cultists. You do love Chaos Cultists don't you?? Though I think they are generic enough to work for most human sized miniatures in any grim and dark dystopian future setting from undercity gangs, to wasteland scavengers, rebels, organized criminal thugs, and pretty much any kind of poorly equipped ne'er-do-wells up to no good.

Here are the 12 unique weapons:

-- Axe
-- Club
-- Hammer1
-- Hammer2
-- Knife1
-- Knife2
-- Mace
-- Pick
-- Pipe
-- Scimitar
-- Sword1
-- Sword2

Each weapon comes in three STL variants:
1) weapon by itself
2) weapon held in a right hand
3) weapon held in a right hand (hand has a nub to socket into wrists)

Knife1 and Knife2 have four variants each, two with the blade held normally and two with the blade held ready to stab. You can mirror the weapons with hands on them to create left-handed versions. All total that comes to 68 different options. You can use these files for physical or digital conversions as you see fit. They are also Creative Common Licensed so that you can modify them as you please and then share your own innovations.

Enjoy, and may the Dark Gods favor you.

This revised version of my old Autopistol STL has some subtle changes that I like. I also added a few variants with different hands attached for easy conversions. In a grimdark science fantasy universe such a weapon as this might be found in the hands of chaotic cultists, undercity gang members, Imperial officials, militia troopers, organized criminals, xeno cultists, merchants and their guards, household troops, and many more. For physically converting or digitally remixing miniatures this one pistol has many potential uses.

I made some changes to my existing Autopistol Model 302 STL. I took most of my inspiration for the original design from a couple images I found online. I liked the look overall, though I felt like the end of the barrel was maybe inclined to break off if dropped. So for this version I changed the proportions so that the muzzle break in front of the weapon connected very slightly to the angled front of the forward handgrip on the pistol. Looking at other images online, I also decided to shorten the pistol's ammo magazine. Previously the magazine extended below the pistol grip, but now it stops just short of being equal in length to the pistol grip. The width and height of the pistol remain the same, but I shortened the overall length from 12mm to 11.5mm which I think makes it scaled a bit better for most plastic, resin, and STL miniatures out there.

Here's a link to the original version.

Autopistol - Model 302 -by- Scavvon
https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/game/autopistol-model-302

When servants of the Inquistion must hunt heretics in the dangerous depths of the undercity it never hurts to have some extra firepower. That's were the Servile Cyborg with Sizable Gun comes in. This single-minded automaton can pack as much firepower as a crew served heavy weapon team. He never complains, but he rarely takes any initiative either. In fact, he performs best with a bit of guidance from his friends. He can be equipped with a selection of three devastating heavy weapons depending on your needs. The ODV Heavy Blaster launches bursts of high caliber dual-mode projectiles that are equally effective against armored or unarmored targets. One shot from this weapon is more than enough to deal with a measely chaotic cultist. The opposite end of the spectrum is the mighty Multi-Mazer Melta-Beamer. This weapon hits just one target, but it hits extremely hard! Definitely a waste when targeting a wimpy chaotic cultist, but hulking mutant abominations or vile places of worship for the followers are the Dark Gods are ideal targets. The final weapon option is the Phased Plasma Projector, this weapon is the happy medium of overkill. It hits like a cargo-8 and covers an area wide enough to catch multiple targets. As an additional benefit this particular Servile Cyborg's Sizable Guns each have unique enhancements to improve their reliability. Because let's face it, there is never a techno-guru around when you need one, let alone when you are in the heart of darkness battling heretics.

--------------------------------

The Mystical Missionary is a steadfast and zealous henchman ready to serve the God Emperor and any worthy inquisitor in his service. Before his recruitment to the inquisition this individual traveled the galaxy visiting any and all human worlds to spread the the God Emperor's light. He has been exposed to many different sects and devotions who all worship the God Emperor. He has witnessed miracles, received divine knowledge from secretive cults, and also his own God Emperor touched visions. The Mystical Missionary is a proven fighter, especially against the forces of Chaos. Though his greatest strengths are his exemplary faith in the God Emperor, his inspirational presence, and his profound knowledge of esoteric mysteries.

Vest is edited to remove rifle ammo pouches. which would make little sense for machinegunners.

Ammo belts are intended to be glued onto a strip of thick paper and then shaped by breaking the links between individual bullets as needed. Two variants of different thickness provided, to make the links breakable at different scales. Let me know how it goes. :)

Two arms posed to hold the ammo belt feeding the minigun are also provided.

I have aso built a minigun backpack from scratch. It has a version without the tubes and handle, if you want to make those out of wire instead.

And yes, bald head and facial hair are mandatory for UAC heavy weapon operators.

Some of you know I did Jenova a while back. Well I wanted the whole crew but the only one I found was low poly, or the collection listed below which is nice but I wanted a bit more detail. About half of this project is a remix, I did check and am allowed to remix the parts I did use. Huge shoutout to the original sculptors.


For those wanting these but don't have a 3d printer, you can use a print service.


Here are the parts I used in the remix because I don't trust thingi to actually list them on the side:

Vincents gun

Aeris Rod
https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:4373049

Chocobo
https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:3973745

Tifa
https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:3831748

Original Models I used parts from
https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:4630558

What was done with each model:

Tifa: Tifa was basically untouched as the original is amazing and stood in for a quality control standard

Chocobo: I thickend the feathers a bit so they print easier

Cait Sith: I cleaned up the stuffed animal part a little and made new wings for it.

Red XII: Cleaned up and leveled out a bit

The others were pretty much only used as an example for the pose.

The sculpting on:

Cid
Sephiroth
Cloud
Cait Sith (the cat portion)
Vincent (other than his gun)
Aeris (other than rod)
Yuffie
Barret
Jenova

were all done by me.

Chaos Cultist #11 Heavy Specialist with BIG Stubber

Recently I released "Chaos Cultist #1" and now I'm releasing this big burly brute with a big gun. And you ask, "What happened to Chaos Cultists #2 through #10?" Well, I skipped them for now. I wanted to make a standout cultist that had a bit more gravitas then just a bunch more basic cultists. I do plan to release Chaos Cultists #2 through #10 and more, just no promises on what order they arrive in.

[UPDATE 2023-06-19] I wanted to fine tune a few things on this miniature. I increased the size of the Big Stubber's barrel because it looked to thin and wimpy on the tabletop to me. I raised the height of the two wrenches on the miniature's backpack so that they have more support and should be more sturdy. I've printed them fine before, but if I'm in a hurry when removing the supports I have also torn off the ends. I also added a bit of thickness to the ammo belt that hangs from the Big Stubber (it's on the backside and not noticeable, paint it like the links in the ammo belt). I've printed models with much thinner parts including ammo belts, but I would like to make my designs as robust and hassle free as possible. Enjoy.

The chaos cultist who would go on to become known as Daemonlash was a solitary and taciturn individual. Despite his reserved manner this cultist was a skilled warrior and a gifted leader. One day he challenged the leader of his chaos cult to a fight to see who would lead the cult. He was handily defeated by the current cult leader. A certain amount of shame came with being thus defeated, but a more serious problem came with this development. The existing cult leader now saw this cultist as a potential threat, maybe he would make a challenge again one day and win. Everyone in the cult knew that their cult leader would almost certainly maneuver things so that his most recent challenger was never a threat again. Knowing this, the defeated challenger volunteered to become a living host for a warp daemon. As a barely sane living weapon for the Dark Powers the former cultist was no longer a threat to the cult leader's position, but at least he was alive.

The daemon that possessed the cultist who would become known as Daemonlash had a peculiar way of not making any outward changes to his host's physical body. Only when in combat would the daemon transmute his host's flesh in the form of grotesque fleshy tentacles that suddenly burst from the cultist's chest. These tentacles shot forward with explosive speed to entangle, rend, and strangle his foes. At these times the cultist's head would also transform to a ghastly cackling daemonic visage. And thus was born the daemon-infused mutant cultist know as 'Daemonlash.'

The cultist who would go on to be known as 'Talon' was scrawny and puny. He was constantly being bullied by the local thugs and gangers in his poor neighborhood. He joined a chaotic cult in hopes of a better life and to escape the foul treatment of his tormentors. Alas, he found that he had only traded one set of bullying torturers for another, for in the chaotic cult strength and power were prized and weakness reviled. The cultist sought out the legendary Master of Possession, Faustus Daemoncaller who was at that time visiting his world in secret. Daemoncaller was only too happy to perform the dreadful and perverse ritual upon the young seeker.

Once joined with the daemon it learned of his past experience and history. Perhaps it was compassion that made the daemon within him transform his body into a massive and brutishly muscled thing with one oversized arm ending in a savage claw. Or perhaps the daemon sensing the dark emotions of it's host, his rage, hatred, and sense of weakness that the daemon fed upon and transformed the young cultist into a form ideal for enacting bloody revenge on all those who had previously plagued him.

After that the cultist earned the name Talon based on his new form and his keen desire to maliciously destroy any who gained his ire. Not long after the old neighbor where Talon was raised became the site of a series of brutal and savage murders which continued for weeks only to end as suddenly as they had began. The unknown perpetrators, or perpetrator, was never identified or apprehended.

[UPDATE 23-01-16] I was not satisfied with the scale and proportions of my first four mutants. So I have uploaded a new STL in a more 'Heroic Scale.' The original version has been retained in a sub-folder.

There is something about cultists of all kinds, they just love their slug throwing stubbers, especially the Big Stubber. What can you say, it's just iconic? Would any of them really be worth calling cultists if they didn't have their Big Stubbers? I've decided to build an army of Frateris Militia led by an Apostate Cardinal. Let's be honest, Frateris Militia are basically imperial cultists. And as such, they will need their own Big Stubbers, lots of Big Stubbers.

I started with LoggyK's excellent Heavy Gun for this design and I just kept adding details until I had the look of a xeno-cultist Big Stubber. The final model is sort of a mix of old and new. The scale should be 1-1.

This model wouldn't have been possible without the talent and generosity of LoggyK.

This is a digital 3D printable model of a Mage. Or a king. It’s up to you. The heads, hands, chests, arms, and legs are completely modular and you can switch them as you progress in your character’s story and equip it with different weapons, spells, and accessories.

**The download contains:**
4x head
4x legs
1x base
3x chest
6x arms
Hands wielding different objects
Accessories such as a cloak and a backpack

All pieces of the model are ready to be 3D printed on an SLA printer. They are prepared for inserting cylindrical magnets.

**Magnets we use:**
Diameter 2 mm
Height 0.90 mm

You might be interested also in **2 Sets of Condition markers for DnD**
Funny Modular: https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/various/funny-magnetic-condition-markers-for-dnd-figures
Practical rings and bases: https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/various/practical-condition-markers-for-dnd-figures

**SIZE**
At 100% scale the mage’s dimensions are approximately:
Width: 35 mm
Height: 40 mm
Base diameter: 25mm
Neck diameter: 3.10 mm
Lower body diameter: 6.30 mm

You can scale the model as you wish.

**ASSEMBLY**
The holes in the models are prepared for inserting magnets (2mm diameter, 0.90 mm high)

This model is meant to be post-processed after printing. This means inserting magnets, and painting.
Printing settings will vary greatly depending on your specific printer.

Learn how to cut your own figures and prepare them for magnets in our Youtube tutorial:
https://youtu.be/A6QtOraIAfQ

Do you like the model and don't have a 3D printer? There are lots of people who offer 3D printing services these days. Try searching for someone who offers them in your area.

This model for Dungeons and Dragons tabletop gaming was brought to life by 3Demon. We are a group of modeling and 3d printing enthusiasts based in Prague, Czech Republic.
We’ve been making 3D printable models for more than a decade. We make a lot of cosplay accessories but we also make all sorts of interesting 3D models.
You can join our community or just look at more of our creations here: https://3d-mon.com/links

This is my entry for the next [28mag challenge](https://28-mag.com/2021/01/12/the-28magchallenge-for-2021/).

Beltanya Zukhal is a legal clerc of the Administratum whose task is to record anything and everything, from dead fluotubes to Astra Militarum empty Autocannon cases and daily casualty on the battlefield. She even records the number of downloads of her STL template.
As part of her missions, she frequently goes on field trips to accompany Regimental HQ staff (where she carries a sidearm for self defence).

It is on one of such missions that she met with Inquisitor Johevian of the Ordo Aegis. Now she works for him undercover and has even been sighted with him as part of his retinue.

As always, "Watch" if you want to be informed of any updates.

In the vast world of 40k exist a myriad of various marks, patterns and types of humble lasgun, and, as usual, GW had forgot about most of them. Fine, I'll do it myself. Plasma weapons are extremely effective at close to medium range. Together with kinetic damage, it transfers significant thermal damage to the target. At close range, this weapon has a chance to damage even heavy armored vehicles. During the Last War, plasma weapons were widespread among the Shapers.

Despite its high efficiency, this weapon has its drawbacks. The lethality of the weapon decreases significantly with distance. The design of this weapon is quite complex, which requires a high production culture and careful maintenance. And in case of malfunctions, self-detonation of the weapon is quite possible.

Jet weapons became widespread during the Last War. The ammunition of this weapon is accelerated by a jet stream. It has practically no recoil, and ammunition can hit a wide variety of targets. Cumulative and armor-piercing ammunition can easily cope with light enemy vehicles. Ammunition with programmable detonation will not leave any chance for the infantry, even in cover.

However, this weapon also has a number of disadvantages. It is quite heavy and for long-term use it is necessary to have exo-armor or genetic modifications. It is also extremely ineffective at close ranges, since the ammunition does not have time to pick up the required speed.

The weapon can be equipped with various magazines. To improve the accuracy of fire, it is possible to install an elongated barrel. Installation of an optical sight is also possible.

11 unique heads

I wanted some alien raiders for playing [Grim Horizons](https://www.wargamevault.com/product/336867/Grim-Horizons--Adventures-Told-Through-Combat) so I made this remix from some available models. The figures are approximately 30mm tall without any base so should get scaled if they are not being used as medium characters.

Modular kit includes rifles, carbines, shotguns, pistols, melee weapons, grenades, and various special weapons.

Note: users will need to mirror some arms and Zip files are used for organisation.

If you enjoy these models please consider [tipping me a coffee](https://www.paypal.me/dotplot1) to encourage creation of new designs and improving existing ones.

Unfortunately the Thingiverse remix source files system is broken at the moment so the remix files are just linked here, I will update this when the systems starts working again.

Here is my first Samurai Daiymo, general, or warlord ready to lead his troops at 10mm scale across the battlefield. As per warmaster, this has a 25mm round base to hold the general and his attendants. He is attended by a Samurai giving him his Katana and a standard bearer holding his Nobori.

I had to go far away from dwarves for some times and I decided to start some models for the High Elf Army. Many models we can find on website are either PLA friendly and ugly or Resin printer made and beautiful.

I worked on a very well known resin model to extract whatever I could use and complete with other stuff. Heads are printed separately and the result is quiet nice. It permits to give some randomness to the unit. Hopefully, High Elf Armies are somehow very strict in their appearance and uniforms (like in the Lord of the Rings in which Elves even move at the same time in a coherent ballet).
Swords need some works with sandpaper or stuff like that for a better shape result as they are very thin.

The whole unit was hard to paint because of the tiny details everywhere but it deserved a clean treatment.

PS: the standard is handmade.

Beltanya Zukhal is a legal clerc of the Administratum whose task is to record anything and everything, from dead fluotubes to Astra Militarum empty Autocannon cases and daily casualty on the battlefield. She even records the number of downloads of her STL template.
As part of her missions, she frequently goes on field trips to accompany Regimental HQ staff (where she carries a sidearm for self defence).

It is on one of such missions that she met with Inquisitor Johevian of the Ordo Aegis. Now she works for him undercover and has even been sighted with him as part of his retinue.

As always, "Watch" if you want to be informed of any updates.

***UPDATE: 2020-08-18***
I uploaded revised models. After printing and receiving feedback from others, I modified the designs to make the models thicker. The models should now be sturdier, making it easier to trim away supports and play with the models without ankles and halberd hafts snapping.
*******************************

I remixed a pile of files from Thingiverse, mostly from EvilFrog (whose stuff is great!), in order to make a full regiment of Empire halberdier strips for the game Warmaster. These are 10mm scale, and would work for late medieval / renaissance troops as well, though nobody fought with a halberd and a shield historically, as a halberd takes two hands to wield. I also included a 40x20x2mm unit base. I highly recommend printing these strips in resin, with supports, at 0.025mm layer height. That's what I plan to do.

Come support these models over on [Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/WGraves)
**Buy my time, Not my models.**

Near future combat (or not) drones at 1/100 (15mm). Designed to print on a filament printer so you can bend the fans to suit, I don't have a resin printer but I don't think resin will bend like that, I may be wrong. These are shown in the photograph next to a rebelminis 15mm operator in red, and a plastic soldier company 15mm WW2 German for scale.

These are freakishly small to trim and assemble. The little dot attached to the back of the guns is there to fold over and act as a standoff from the drone body.

I would suggest just printing the "drones sampler" file as it makes 1 of each size and type of drone, all the bases, and 3 sets of weapons.

"As soon as the fortress walls are breached, the specialists rush into battle. Armed with Powered swords, and Shielding technology integrated into their ornate Titan-Ferrum shield, they cut away any opposition easily, and clear the way for the rest of the army!"

Close Combat specialists in the style of the Hostile Environment Guardsmen. each part is seperate (a first for my models), which allows greater customization and posing options.
All parts have been scaled correctly and are ready to print.

The helmet fits into the torso, via a roughly 4mm circular joint, and should therefore also allow you to use other existing bits you might have lying around.

No legs included.

"Each crackle of their rifles, was a death sentence to their enemies. Their old rifles had been replaced for this mission, and the soldiers had been eager to try out the fresh forge-crafted laser rifles. The normal magazines had been exchanged for a power cable, hooked up to the proto-fusion capacitators on their back; standard issue for their regiment; allowing them a much higher rate of fire, and fewer reloads than normal"

3 different variants of snipers intended for 28mm wargaming, in line with the rest of the Hostile Environment Guardsmen I've made, and also includes a standalone sniper rifle. Due to popular requests, I made sure that the cables were much thicker and wider this time, to make them easier for printing and painting.
This is also one of the few times I'll be using legs (by ZioCru, go check out his stuff), as I intend for the models I make to be used as conversion pieces, and not wholly printed models.

Enjoy!

Hello and welcome to the scifi heavy weapons collection!

These aren't the most beautiful or elegant weapons, but they ought to go nicely with your existing plastic models for maximum destruction of enemies large and small.

These are remixed from... loads of stuff I had laying around, including stuff from LoggyK, Landon73, and SebTheis. If I used a bit of yours and your name's not on that list, sorry! Please let me know!

**Printing Notes!** I haven't tested these extensively, and I only printed them in resin, so I have no idea what problems might exist. Please let me know if there are problems, and I can try to fix them for a future version.

This is a reupload as the original wasn't showing up under my designs, and I also wanted to add another version, with the sword in a resting position and a bionic arm.

"He looked over the horizon, he'd grown accustomed to the ash wastes of Teidon Prime, just like he had with the endless swamps of Delta-64-91. He'd been on countless worlds, each a different home, with different families. Families he'd soon depart with, as he once again would be the only one out of the warzone. He gave a fake smile to the corporal next to him, who smiled back unknowingly that the sergeant had done the same to last 3 men and women assigned to him. "another warzone corporal, another battle to win. Remember your training, and I'll make sure you'll be back home with your family in a couple of months". He donned his mask and yelled orders for the charge, already having said goodbye to those around him"

This is a single model, meant to represent either a veteran sergeant or higher ranking officer of the Hostile Environment Guardsmen.
He's armed with a powered sword, plasma pistol and improved armour against shrapnell.

Remixed from the following parts:
Heroic scale heads for wargaming miniatures 28mm. By Brexit: https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:3217411

Hostile Environment Guardsmen; Plasma Pistol and Powered Sword. By Cikkirock(me): https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:4657887
https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:4693247

Angry Spaceguard Legs; Angry Spaceguard Arms clean. By ZioCru:
https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:4582571
https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:4580213

Special Thanks to ZioCru for feedback during the creation process

Hey folks!

Here are some Gambesons for your kitbashing projects. I will be posting a set of characters donning it soon (I tried to keep it functional and interesting)

Technical Details:
Functional chest piece open in the front (no need for helper to put it on) made of a short skirted and short sleeved historical inspired gambeson.

DnD Armor type: Padded Armor. I have kept it short to represent the low level of protection described in the PhB. In reality these armors rock! Some say they are more protective and overall better than leather (I am looking at you Shad and Skallagrim).

Hope you enjoy it!

Let me know in the comments what you would like to get next!

These 15 player character models are collected from various free posts we've made over the years, and come with character record sheets for our [CRUX roleplaying system, which is available as a free download from our own site](http://www.illgottengames.net/cruxuniversalroleplaying), as well as rules for [Pocket-Tactics](http://www.illgottengames.net/pocket-tactics) (our 3d pint-and-play strategy board game) and [Open-Tactics](http://www.illgottengames.net/opentactics) (our open-source, miniatures-agnostic wargaming rules).

All models are supplied without bases and print 100% support free. Daring Delvers are scaled for standard miniature gaming (30mm scale), and 15mm versions are included as well! Blank bases are included for both scales and, if you want a quick tutorial on adding them before printing, [check out this video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HGCwjUJVZ-0).

For those of you thinking about [supporting us on Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/illgottengames?fan_landing=true), our patrons get special weekly model releases, access to new storefront releases and our entire back catalog, plus licensing options to sell printed versions of our designs.

"The drenched wetlands of Cerabo IV poses many dangers, after a millenia of fighting, the once abundant flora of this world has turned into a toxic nightmare. 
Only with the right equipment do soldiers still march across the battlefield, to deliver justice to their enemies."


Updated 19-11-2020:
since so many people seem to like my remix, I've added a few more variants to the roster.
including a... WIP? female sergent, using the head of Toawi's Soldier Female: https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:4596304/files

the different body options has the heads facing FL(left), FR(right), FF(front).

A remix of LoggyK's torso and kasrkin helmet, combined into one, and also a standalone backpack of my own doing. 
I pumped up the armour pieces a bit, to make them stand out more, and added a skull by Der_Graue
https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:2396869

Included is also a radio version, which can fit a 0.5mm wire piece as an antennae.

The skull on the front has a small slope to help with printing.

To replace the mis-scaled original Mantic Basilean Men-at-Arms arms.

I had 80 of the original MAA Basileans with the terribly oversized gorilla arms. I put these together to replace the sword and shield arm and they scale well and look pretty good. When I got these originally I was so disappointed that I shelved the entire army years ago without assembling anything. Now, I can get excited about this great army again!

I also created a spear version with longer shields.

I wanted to use the original Mantic shields, but it was so much work removing the original arm, so I thought these shields would fit the Basileans nicely. Not recommended for FDM printing. I printed on mt Elegoo Mars with using only light supports (Auto) and was able to get quite a few sets on the build plate.

The shield is from cncmodels4you (3946113), but for some reason Thingiverse is not letting me add another remix source - will try to again to add later on.

I had in mind the picture of fat friars and fighter-monks in dresses and I wanted to be able to customize each minis but with a unique body basis.

I uploaded revised models. After printing and receiving feedback from others, I modified the designs to make the models thicker. The models should now be sturdier, making it easier to trim away supports and play with the models without ankles and halberd hafts snapping.

These are 10mm scale, and would work for late medieval / renaissance troops as well, though nobody fought with a halberd and a shield historically, as a halberd takes two hands to wield. I also included a 40x20x2mm unit base. I highly recommend printing these strips in resin, with supports, at 0.025mm layer height. That's what I plan to do.

Hey folks! Just 3 parts for you to place in your miniatures to customize your characters. Extra thick to increase compatibility. Heavily based in historic milanese armor (high waist large shoulder piece, few folds)
My process to adapt them (blender 2.8+):
1- Load your miniature and the armor parts
2- Place them more or less in position
3- Get the best fit you can simply scaling it (if some parts of the mini stick out, don't worry, get the overall placement)
4 - Try sculpting down (elastic deform brush in blender works wonders!) the parts sticking out in the original mini.
5- Use the sculpting elastic deform to give the final touches.

It normally takes less than 5 min for even somewhat complex models!

Hope you enjoy it!

Thingiverse is broken and I cannot add any current links to the remixes, as soon as it's fixed I will add all the information in. Sorry for the inconvenience. 

NOTE: Every part except the backpacks and helmets should be printed at about 85% scale. Do a test print beforehand to make sure that they are scaled correctly to a primaris. They shouldn't excede 40mm in height.

Inspired by the great art of Mo Mukhtar https://www.artstation.com/artwork/RYxAbO

I decided to give it a go and design a 3d printable model kit to host your very own Asta'Vesa soldiers. 

This time I am working only on my own idea with creating a Apothecary equivalent for the Asta'Vesa. These are one of the most important people involved in running an Astarted Force and I cannot imagine Tau Managing to sustain any astartes force without the Apothecaries maintiaining their medical needs. 

Ladies and Gentleman: meat the Apothecary.

They aren't as close to the fanart as I'd like but then again, they are designed to retain their character when being printed as a 28 milimiter scale models so I needed to exagerate some features and smooth out some details and I used some preexisting model sculpts and heavily modified them.

As always, please don't use this kit commercially. This is a gift from me to the community.
However if you would like to tip me, my tip link is https://paypal.me/elmutanto
But this is totally optional and the files are free to download and use non-commercially.

Hope you guys will like this. It was a blast to work on them.

Ulf Mausschnauze was a rat catcher of great renown. As his eyesight deteriorated significantly after years spent in the sewers, he hired his personal lantern bearer, Jim. However, Jim's light was a clear sign for the rats to hide, Ulf became less effective and Jim was fired. Don't worry, Jim was soon hired as a town guard on night shifts.

Suitable for 28mm tabletop games.
Created so that it does not need any supports and prints well on a cheap FDM 3d printer like the Ender 3.
There are variants with square and round bases.

Unsatisfied with my earlier set of loincloths, I got drunk and set to work. This is the product of my labor. These are flippable, resizeable, to cover loins or do whatever you want with. should work wonderfully for salamanders but also for any other chapters that feature scaled greebly things. I am working on scaled drapes for shoulder pads next so watch out for those. I've printed a couple and the detail is very nice at 0.08 layer height on a stock nozzle, with clearly printed scales and hammers. Print vertically with a small raft (3-5mm is great) for added stability. Printing horizontally works too but scales will be rounder/messier.

Note: can't speak for you resin bois but for FDM printers the smaller studs WILL NOT PRINT. Thus, I hastily added the three larger studs that do.

Hello! these "high" poly models have been designed for those who are learning, or want to start learning 3D modelling and make their very own miniatures. Its a place holder, or a very basic tool i provide to already start tweaking around, making poses, facial expresions, simple stuff as you keep learning from tutorials in the internet.

They have been designed with heroic proportions: thick hand and foot, bigger head, a medium volume muscle mass (so you can add more muscle/fat or remove volume easily to make a skinny character).

The MALE human has 6 heads tall. The head is 5mm in heigth, and he is 30mm tall (28mm to eyes).

For reference, each square of the GRID is 1x1mm.

I provide a 30x30mm grid and 3 images explaining basic stuff needed to know how and why do certain things regarding importing-exporting files in zBrush. Similar process is needed for other modelling softwares but i only use zBrush.

:::::::::::::

WORKFLOW

If you already know a bit how to use zbrush, now, you have to:

Duplicate the subtool (body in this case) select one of them (hide the original) to make Zremesh, all times neceasry to have aprox 3-5k polys.

Then subdivide about 4 times.

Then activate the original hidden model while still having selected the one you zremeshed (which now is looking smooth and with lot less of details) and select PROJECT.

SO, the details on the original model, will project into the remeshed+subdivided model polys,and woila! now you have the model with multiple levels ofpolys, from 5k to about 1millon.

Now you have a model to POSE in the low poly level and when you are happy, you apply DYNAMESH and start sculpting! (after finishing sculpting you will have to decimate the model, in average a foot miniature like human/elve/orc is around 100K polys)

HEre is an example of how to pose a low poly model:

youtube.com/watch?v=s6THhnv0m6g&fbclid=IwAR18aXLSvvSM9S9y-CkW3kSOtdEgZgrbM_mFq15ockUKAV9Hi6M1iJcRLCE

Cya!

Erramir Orlans.

"Rat Rogue! He's ready to plunder the nearest dungeon of loot, sack at the ready to haul it back in! Perfect for homebrew races like Ratfolk, Ratkin, etcetera."

My first sculpt was fairly early on in my Blender learning experience, and I like to think that I've improved a little bit since then, so I decided to add a little more detail to it. Broke out the sword from the amazing Bloody Glorious Hawk Boy model to use as a spiritual weapon for a DND Cleric character and got a lot of requests to post the STL. Recommend printing on a resin printer. If you have a really well dialed in FDM printer you can try printing the file as it's imported with supports to have the best chance of getting the flames to come out. Might not be a bad idea to scale up to 110 or 120% for FDM to give the fine details a better chance.

Once printed simply glue it to your favorite base model which can easily be printed in FDM or resin. Here's one of my favorite packs:
https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:3675552

Description :

We at Ill Gotten Games are big fans of the [Vintage RPG Podcast](https://www.stitcher.com/podcast/unwinnable-3/the-vintage-rpg-podcast), and after designing a model for Hambone [the hammer-wielding ranger, Johan](https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:3483772)), I made one for Stu as well. This is Greel, an opportunistic (but deep down, gold-hearted) ex-mercenary company leader/current warlock with a magic ring that can turn him into a tree at the first sight of danger. The model prints without support.

If you haven't checked it out, Hambone and Stu (Horvath, from [unwinnable.com](https://unwinnable.com/)) do a weekly podcast where they discuss tabletop games, and do deep dives into RPGs old and new. This all branches off of Stu's excellent [Instagram feed](https://www.instagram.com/vintagerpg/?hl=en), which is always an insightful read if you're into the history and current state of tabletop roleplaying games. We're proud to be [supporting them on Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/vintagerpg/overview), and you should really check out what they're doing/throw them some bones if you like it as much as we do.

Description :

Even within the dogmatic and zealous organisation, that is the Cult of Machines, few can hope to match the fanatism of these monks, who are going so far as to invite the frightening might of the kinetic force into their very own bodies until their skin cracks and their eyes boil in their sockets under the electrical inferno. But the rewards for the faithful far outweigh such petty losses as sight and sense of touch, as they are able to stride into the apocalyptic battlefields of the future almost naked, untouchable by deadly projectiles and shrapnels, for the kinetic force shields their own from the attacks of the unenlightened in a shroud of lightning. And in turn each strike of the arcane weapons of these pilgrims leaves enemies and heretical warmachines alike lying cold and dead, as their bioelectricity is absorbed from their unworthy bodies.

I always felt a certain affection to this model series, since they were some of my very first models. Now, with six good ones, which carry enough bits to remix a squad of twenty if necessary, I feel like a can put them aside for the time being Hope you are as content with them as I am.

Starting today, we're launching "Monster Mondays," a regular feature where we upload a new monster miniature design to our online [storefront](http://www.illgottengames.net/products/?category=Miniatures), with our [Patreon supporters](https://www.patreon.com/illgottengames) getting free access. Each unique character will include RPG rules for our own D6Modular system (currently in beta for our patrons) and rules compatible with 5E Dungeons & Dragons.

First up, we're including Baymara, the Grand Chronicler of High Hivald. Though not technically a monster, she'll be the narrator of our growing monster compendium, and you can consider this "entry zero." (We'll be posting the first official monster entry to Thingiverse later today.) As with all of our upcoming monster designs, Baymara prints without need of support on FDM printers.

For those of you supporting us (or thinking about supporting us) on [Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/illgottengames), our patrons get special access to our store releases as they come out (not to mention license options to sell printed versions of our designs).

Enjoy!

-Character art is by the talented [Benjamin Honeycutt](https://www.artstation.com/benhoneycutt)

After the fall of the Council, the Great Hunt was unleashed against anyone who seemed fit for the arcane. During these dark times, the Assassins emerged as a force of balance. "Assassination" was the term by which the vulgar referred to an unresolved crime; an Assassin was that individual capable of committing a crime and never be discovered. Little by little, their presence was becoming more frequent during the Great Hunt: people who tortured children during the night appeared dead in the morning; judges who condemned the innocent were found hanged and with horrible marks on their bodies.

In her quest for balance, the Assassin searchs within the Dark Wizard's domains looking for the means to restore Magic to it's rightfull place... and becoming a more lethal weapon against all who opose the arcane.

I wasn't intending on doing a follow up piece to my previous sculpt, but got inspired by beardly goodness.

Character sculpt at relatively low, medium and high and highest poly counts.

File will need support material, but the top half of the model has been successfully printed on an UP printer, needing relatively low amount of supports. Should work great on a resin/SLA printer. Hoping to do a full test print soon, will see if a manually modelled support structure is needed for the hair. Was just too keen to make the file public and see what the community does with it. :)

Edit: Confirmed printable on FDM! Thanks ichibey!

Edit 2: Uploaded second option for all detail levels with a single shell, mostly to fix issues with the eyes. Thanks 3DWP! Zip file contains all detail levels.

Sculpted in Zbrush, preview renders in Blender, final check and stl file saved from Netfabb.

Approximate poly counts
Low = 137,000 tris
Med = 372,000 tris
High = 965,000 tris
Highest = 2,804,000 tris

On the now inhospitable world of Eden 2, human settlers have largely relocated into the vast subterranean complex known colloquially as Tunnel World. In this labyrinthine world, the fixit men co-opt junk gathered from the toxic surface into useful devices, vehicles, and weapons, honoring the ways of the Ancestors.

Character for a Continuum RPG scenario, modeled in Sculptris and TinkerCAD for 28mm scale gaming.

Formerly a blaster for a prolific dwarven mining company, Ralph Siggurdson eschewed his clan code and went rogue, joining the trans-universal mercenary unit known as Baker's Dozen. Since the surviving Dozen retired and went their separate ways, Ralph was last seen relic hunting in Tunnelworld, the vast, labyrinthine complex sprawling beneath the waste-world of Eden 2.

Ralph is modeled in 54mm scale and is an RPG character created by thingiverse user Foolsgmbit and modeled by myself
